Article Title: Oil prices fall $1 after touching three week high amid Middle East tensions
Article Text:
Crude prices steady after touching three week high

Oil prices fell by more than $1 in early trade on Thursday as investors weighed threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against the possibility of the US easing sanctions on oil-carrying vessels.Brent crude dropped 1.30% to $104.70, shedding $1.38, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 1.07% to $94.07, a decline of $1.02.The decline followed a sharp rise in WTI in the previous session, when prices reached a three-week high. The rally came after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran announced new tactics to target vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, with the stated aim of keeping oil prices high.The threat to maritime traffic remained elevated. Two vessels: a container ship and a dry bulk carrier, sank near the strait within 24 hours after separate projectile strikes, maritime officials said on Wednesday.Attacks in the surrounding waters have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying its strikes in retaliation for the US blockade of Iranian ports and the tougher sanctions imposed last month.The disruption caused by the Iran war has pushed freight costs to record highs, prompting the Trump administration to consider easing restrictions on vessels used to transport oil from sanctioned countries.A US official said on Wednesday that the administration was considering sanctions relief for so-called shadow fleet vessels, which have carried oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela. The move is aimed at helping reduce petroleum shipping costs.Furthermore, rising oil production and exports from Russia and the Middle East have also helped contain prices amid the supply concerns.Russia's crude oil output increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).However, production remained 870,000 barrels per day lower than a year earlier.The IEA also reported a monthly increase of 4.4 million barrels per day in crude oil exports from Middle East Gulf producers in September. Exports reached around 75% of their prewar levels.Now, the US-Iran conflict has continued for over seven months, keeping oil markets on edge. However, the price spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel levels seen earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude dropped 1.30% to $104.70, shedding $1.38, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 1.07%. The decline followed a sharp rise in WTI in the previous session, when prices reached a three-week high. The rally came after Iran announced new tactics to target vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: MDR on UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 deferred; to come into effect post Diwali
Article Text:
Govt defers 0.4% merchant discount rate on UPI payments

MUMBAI: Its official. There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The National Payment’s Corporation of India’s The UPI and Services Steering Committee has deferred the implementation of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select person-to-merchant UPI transactions until immediately after Diwali, citing the festive season. The implementation date will be notified separately.The Times of India had reported last week that finance ministry and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) have decided to defer the introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions, seeking to avoid adding to business costs and hitting consumption at a time of economic headwinds, people aware of the matter said. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. However,the announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali.The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15, with a 0.4% charge for eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The framework was to take effect from October 15, giving banks, payment aggregators and other ecosystem participants a month to make operational changes.Also read: Pakistan angle under probe? Delhi Police files 4 FIRs over fake posts since Oct 10 The decision to defer the rollout comes just days before the scheduled start and follows demands from trade bodies and merchant associations for a January implementation. They have argued that introducing the fee during the festive season, when retail activity and digital payments typically rise, could increase costs for merchants and weigh on sales.The framework was designed to create a revenue stream for the payments ecosystem after more than six years of effectively zero MDR on UPI. The government had said the levy would apply only to specified merchant transactions, with payments up to Rs 2,000 and eligible small merchants continuing to remain free. About 96% of P2M transactions were expected to remain unaffected.The deferment gives merchants and payment companies more time to prepare while allowing the government to avoid introducing a new transaction cost at a potentially sensitive point for consumption.
Article Summary: There will be no MDR on UPI until the festival season is over. The revised rollout was expected to be pushed to January 2027 from October 15. The announcement on Tuesday states that the implementation will be immediately after Diwali. The MDR framework was approved and notified by NPCI on September 15.

Article Title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY27 and FY28
Article Text:
India's growth story remains strong

India holds its ground despite higher oil prices

World Bank, OECD raise India growth forecasts

Global growth faces a more fragile outlook

India’s economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), keeping the country among the fastest-growing major economies despite growing uncertainties. According to the institution, strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth.India's growth prospects were supported by favourable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms, even as higher oil prices posed a challenge.“India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favorable demographic dynamics, a large and expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms.”The forecast comes amid a series of upgrades by global agencies after India's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter of the current financial year.The agency expects India to remain among the fastest-growing major economies, with domestic demand and services activity helping sustain momentum.“India remains among the fastest-growing major economies, with growth in 2026 projected at 7.0 percent.This reflects stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.”It also highlighted how the Indian economy continued to expand despite rising oil prices. “India’s growth remained robust, underpinned by domestic demand and services, despite higher oil prices.”The improved outlook follows the stronger-than-expected GDP growth recorded in the April-June quarter, prompting several global institutions, including the World Bank, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), S&P Global Ratings, Moody's Ratings, Fitch Ratings and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to raise their growth estimates for India.The World Bank raised its growth projection for India in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.6% estimated earlier. The multilateral agency attributed the revision to strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds. It expects the economy to grow by 7.2% in 2027-28.The OECD has also increased its forecast for India's GDP growth in 2026-27 to 7.1%, from 6.3% projected in June. The revised estimate is higher than the 7% forecasts from S&P, Moody's and ADB, while Fitch expects growth of 6.9%.Moody's Ratings raised its forecast for India's real GDP growth in FY27 to 7%, from 6%, citing the economy's resilience amid the Middle East conflict."Although we continue to expect India to grow faster than all other G-20 economies, as well as similarly rated emerging market sovereigns, risks remain," Moody’s said.Expansion in the April-June quarter was supported by strong investment and manufacturing activity, which helped offset weakness in mining and consumer-facing services.While India has received a series of growth upgrades, the IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.“The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven. Growth is projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while inflation is expected to reach 4.7%, driven largely by higher energy and food prices.”The global outlook also presents risks for India.Higher crude oil and energy prices could fuel inflation and put pressure on household purchasing power. Below-normal monsoon rainfall could affect agricultural output and rural demand, while prolonged geopolitical tensions could disrupt supply chains and increase input costs.Despite the upward revisions to India's growth projections, these factors remain among the risks flagged by agencies assessing the country's economic outlook.
Article Summary: India's economy is expected to grow by 7% in both 2026 and 2027. Strong domestic demand, robust services activity and favourable demographic trends are expected to support this growth. The IMF has warned that the global economy's resilience is becoming increasingly fragile and uneven.

Article Title: 'Big items are done': Sergio Gor gives update on India-US trade deal, Trump's 100% sanctions threat
Article Text:
Sergio Gor

India-US trade deal: ‘ big items are done’

US firms and their Indian presence

US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor on Thursday said the two countries had wrapped up the major items on their trade deal agenda, with negotiations moving at an “incredible pace”. Drawing a comparison with the India-EU trade pact, Gor highlighted the speed of the US talks, saying a deal was announced within weeks of his arrival in India, while negotiations for the European Union agreement took nearly two decades.Commenting on America’s 100% tariff for Russian gas and oil buyers, he said that US President Donald Trump is expected to take a decision within the next 10 days. Gor said that the legislation, which received 86 votes in the 100-member US Senate, gives the President the authority to impose sanctions on countries involved in buying Russian oil and gas or helping others evade sanctions. However, he maintained that the measures were not designed to target India or any other individual country.“...We have ongoing discussions on that as it passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. That law got 86 votes out of 100 in our Senate... These sanctions options that Congress passed, they are not targeted at any individual country. It is three different buckets; one is oil, the second is gas, the third is sanctions evasion.”He further added that these nations are identified based on numbers.“It just happens that India does fall in one of those buckets, along with a lot of other countries.The goal is not to punish anyone. The goal is to try to bring an end to this war. I do think the president will make a determination on that over the next few days...”The law requires Trump to make a determination within 30 days of its passage. Gor said that no country had yet been sanctioned under the legislation and that any decision on exemptions or relief for India would be up to the President.“He has to make a determination in the next I believe 10 or so days,” Gor said.Alongside the discussions on sanctions, Gor expressed confidence that India and the US would soon reach a trade agreement, saying the negotiations had advanced considerably despite the challenges involved.“The big picture, the big framework, the big items are done,” he said, describing the outstanding matters as smaller details and issues that could arise as talks continued.The negotiations have now been under way for around a year and a half.Gor said that the pace of discussions compared favourably with other trade agreements, while noting that the US had to revisit parts of an earlier arrangement after the Supreme Court ruled the law underpinning it unconstitutional.He pointed to the speed of engagement since his arrival in India as a reason for optimism, contrasting the process with the time taken to negotiate the European Union trade deal.“...Within three weeks of arriving here, we announced a trade deal... The European Union trade deal took almost 20 years. So we're at an incredible pace, and I am confident that we will get it done.”Gor said that American businesses had significant opportunities in India, thanks to the country's market and government's approach to overseas investment. He highlighted defence manufacturing, IT, data centres and chip manufacturing as areas where companies from the two countries were already working together.“...You have an unmatched market here for our companies... For the private sector to be able to come to India to compete, to have their foot in the door, you have a very pragmatic prime minister here that welcomes outside investment. Pick any sector, and we're working together at it.”Naming the sectors where India excels, the US ambassador said, “If you look at the defence world, we have co-production happening here in India. If you look at IT, it's unmatched. Google, Microsoft, Adobe, Micron; every one of them is opening data centres and chip manufacturing here that work with our companies hand in hand in the United States. So when a job is created in India, a counter job is created in the United States. It is an incredible win-win situation that I would say is unmatched. We're actively engaged...”According to Gor, investment in India can generate employment opportunities on both sides, with US companies working alongside their American counterparts even as they expand operations in India. He added that the two countries were actively engaged across sectors and reiterated his confidence in the trade negotiations.
Article Summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said the two countries had wrapped up the major items on their trade deal agenda. He said that US President Donald Trump is expected to take a decision within the next 10 days. Gor expressed confidence that India and the US would soon reach a trade agreement.

Article Title: 12,700 US-based tech professionals returned to India in 9 months; 2026 may beat last year's record as H-1B visa uncertainty grows, but returnees face steep salary cuts at home
Article Text:
The growing flow of returnees could eventually leave India with a net gain in technology talent from the US. (Image for representative purpose only)

Indian techies return from the US

Job issues

Thousands of US-based Indian techies are returning to India to a job market that does not offer similar salary levels. But, the number of such returnees is increasing as visa uncertainties weigh under the Donald Trump administration.As the number of technology professionals returning from the US continues to rise, India could be heading towards a reversal in the movement of talent between the two countries.Between January and September 2026, around 12,700 white-collar technology workers returned to India, according to data sourced from staffing firm Xpheno by ET. The tally is already approaching the record 15,100 returnees recorded in the whole of 2025, and is expected to surpass that figure by the end of this year.The increase has been consistent over the past few years. Xpheno's data puts the number of professionals who moved back to India at 7,200 in 2023, rising to 9,800 in 2024 before reaching last year's peak. The figures cover white-collar technology workers moving in either direction between India and the US, rather than only those travelling on H-1B visas.The growing flow of returnees could eventually leave India with a net gain in technology talent from the US, meaning more professionals would be moving back home than heading there.For now, however, the outbound movement remains higher. Nearly 14,500 people moved from India to the US up to September this year, Xpheno's figures show.Kamal Karanth, cofounder of Xpheno, told the financial daily that the number of technology professionals returning to India this year was on track to exceed the 2025 total, further narrowing the difference between inbound and outbound talent flows.He also indicated that the recent H-1B move could accelerate the shift, potentially pushing the number of returnees above the count of technology professionals leaving India for the US.The changing pattern of migration is partly linked to uncertainty over US immigration rules and economic policies, along with the tightening of visa regulations over the past few years, experts said. Rising layoffs at large technology companies in the US during the last two to three years could also be contributing to the trend.Xpheno's assessment draws on several sources, including its internal database of candidates, its recruitment management system and job boards used for hiring in India and overseas. The staffing firm examines these records from a recruiter's standpoint to identify patterns in cross-border talent movement, professional experience and compensation.Returning to India with years of professional experience does not necessarily make finding a suitable job any easier. The current hiring environment has been particularly difficult for technology professionals coming back from the US, said Kamal Karanth, cofounder of staffing firm Xpheno.“Considering the dynamics and trends of active demand in the Indian job market, it has not been the best of times for US returnees,” Karanth said.He pointed out that the Indian technology sector has struggled to maintain consistent hiring momentum since the surge in recruitment in 2021. “After the hiring buoyancy of 2021, the Indian tech sector’s talent action has not had a period of stability extending beyond a quarter,” he noted.Neeti Sharma, chief executive of staffing firm TeamLease Digital, said companies in India are taking a more selective approach to recruitment. Rather than treating overseas experience as a major advantage, employers are placing greater emphasis on candidates' specialised skills and relevant work experience.According to Sharma, the strongest demand is for professionals with expertise in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, data and product leadership. Skills in cloud computing, cybersecurity and implementing AI solutions across enterprises are also sought after.Pay is another significant hurdle for professionals returning from the US. Depending on their role, employer, location and project experience, many may have to settle for salaries equivalent to just 25% to 33% of what they earned overseas, experts said.Xpheno's data puts the average annual salary of a full-stack engineer working in the US on an H-1B visa at $105,000, with earnings typically ranging from $70,000 to $150,000. In India, however, professionals with comparable skills and experience who rank among the top 1% can earn between $20,000 and $32,000 annually.Indian employers are largely maintaining compensation levels in line with domestic salary structures instead of matching pay packages offered in overseas markets. As a result, professionals returning from the US may need to lower their salary expectations to secure suitable positions.Sharma said applied AI professionals in India can earn annual salaries of around Rs 16 lakh to Rs 35 lakh, equivalent to approximately $16,800 to $36,800. Senior specialists, however, can command significantly higher compensation.Global capability centres (GCCs) in India are another potential source of employment for returning professionals. However, those seeking jobs at these centres must compete with experienced candidates who are already available in the domestic talent pool.
Article Summary: Around 12,700 white-collar technology workers returned to India between January and September 2026. The tally is already approaching the record 15,100 returnees recorded in the whole of 2025. The growing flow of returnees could eventually leave India with a net gain in technology talent from the US.

Article Title: Figma sees design as key differentiator as AI lowers coding barriers: CEO Dylan Field
Article Text:
Figma CEO and cofounder Dylan Field

As AI makes coding faster and lowers the barriers to building software, the value in technology development will increasingly shift towards design, where understanding users, business needs and cultural context will remain critical, Figma CEO and cofounder Dylan Field said.Field, who is visiting India for the first time, said the country’s pragmatic approach to technology adoption stood out compared with San Francisco, where experimentation often generates considerable noise. Indian companies were focused on identifying what would advance their businesses and deliver tangible returns, he said.“Some people here might already be ahead of people in San Francisco. There is a lot of noise there, with people trying a lot of things. Some of those things are great. They will be the future. But there is also a lot of noise that does not work out,” Field said.AI’s ability to perform tasks with verifiable outcomes, such as mathematics, cybersecurity and coding, is advancing rapidly. But designing systems that are maintainable, extensible and aligned with business needs remains more complex, he said. Design involves multiple possible solutions, requiring an understanding of users, culture, business problems and aesthetics.“Design is this combinatorial explosion of options where there is no one right answer,” Field said. “You are trying to connect to the culture, business problems and users. You need to have great empathy. These are not things AI is amazing at.” In 2022, Adobe announced plans to acquire Figma in a $20 billion cash-and-stock deal. However, the proposed acquisition collapsed in December 2023 amid regulatory hurdles.AI-generated content can also struggle to stand out because it often resembles existing work, potentially undermining trust, he said. Products that attract users are those that demonstrate craft, care and intention. Rather than replacing human creativity, AI can provide an initial output that designers refine to reflect their own thinking.Field said this shift would not make engineers redundant. Figma continues to hire engineers who can think through systems rather than merely use AI tools. As AI gets better at translating designs into code, the development process can focus more on exploring alternatives and deciding what to build, rather than only how to build it.Figma is developing tools that allow users to move between design and code on the same canvas, bringing in context from coding agents and specifications. Its Model Context Protocol (MCP) also allows users to take design context into external tools to accelerate development.The company is expanding its India operations, which began about a year ago with go-to-market, sales and customer-support functions. It is now adding designer and developer advocates, with product and engineering potentially following as the team grows.India is a priority market for Figma, with its second-largest daily active user base, Field said. However, supporting customers remains the immediate focus.Figma is also seeking to improve the efficiency of AI-assisted development. Its Code Connect tool maps design systems to components and tokens in code, reducing the need for AI models to search for matching elements. Field said this saves customers 25-33% in token costs.Figma unveiled AI-powered features at Config India in Bengaluru to help design, product and engineering teams collaborate on a shared canvas, build code-backed prototypes and develop websites using real data.The updates include Code Layers for creating and editing prototypes on the design canvas, Figma Specs for aligning teams on product requirements and guiding AI agents, and Payload for building data-backed websites and internal tools.“Customers often tell us they prefer working together with their teams on the canvas rather than alone with coding agents in a terminal or IDE,” Field said. Code Layers is launching in open beta.
Article Summary: Figma CEO and cofounder Dylan Field is visiting India for the first time. He said the country’s pragmatic approach to technology adoption stood out compared with San Francisco. India is a priority market for Figma, with its second- largest daily active user base.

Article Title: Rs 53k crore IDBI stake sale with LIC takes government past selloff target
Article Text:
Fairfax gets 2 yrs to decide on CSB stake

NEW DELHI: Govt and LIC will sell a combined 60.7% in IDBI Bank for Rs 52,878 crore to an arm of Fairfax Financial Holdings, which is controlled by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, that will result in the largest-ever financial sector FDI in the country. The transaction will help govt scale the disinvestment and asset monetisation target of Rs 80,000 crore for the current fiscal year.The Centre will sell 30.48% to 10955230 Canada Inc, while LIC will offload 30.24% after the cabinet committee on economic affairs cleared the transaction on Wednesday, five years after the process started and seven months after the earlier bids by Fairfax and Emirates NBD were rejected. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the "strategic restructuring" - as opposed to strategic sale - will result in govt retaining a 15% stake. LIC will have 19% of the equity capital, which will have to be diluted to 15% in two years as the life insurer is also the promoter of a housing finance company.After signing the share purchase agreement, the Canadian company will have to make an open offer for the 5.3% stake held by the public.Fairfax, which will present its credentials to RBI in the coming weeks, will have to decide on its 40% holding in Catholic Syrian Bank — whether it will sell the shares or merge the bank with IDBI Bank.Over the next 15 years, the Canadian company will be required to pare its stake to 26%. The sale comes with a lock-in period of five years with the Canadian company allowed to retain the brand for three years.Although the decision was announced after the stock market closed, IDBI shares closed 9% higher at Rs 90.44 on BSE. “Having supported the bank’s recovery, we are now enabling its next phase of growth through the infusion of FDI while retaining a minority stake. This will not only strengthen the banking ecosystem but also help banking services surpass global benchmarks. It reinforces that India’s growth story is strong, its economy is resilient, and the government’s commitment to reform is unwavering,” Sitharaman said in a post on X. While strategic sale is part of NDA govt’s policy, before IDBI, there have only been three transactions that went through — Air India (2021-22), Ferro Scrap Nigam (2024) and Indian Medicines Pharmaceuticals Corporation (May 2026).Govt will completely exit the board of the bank after the sale, which was first discussed in 2016, but was put off, before restarting in 2020 with the preliminary information memorandum issued in Oct 2022. From five players, the field narrowed to two, which submitted their bids that were rejected in March as they were below the reserve price of 94.42 a share, influenced by the market price which swung between Rs 42.40 when expression of interest was sought and Rs 108. 12 on Jan 8, before bids were invited. Given the volatility in the narrowly traded scrip, with only 5.3% public holding, govt opted to use relative valuation by the market multiple method. Separately, the asset valuation method was also used.
Article Summary: The Centre will sell 30.48% to 10955230 Canada Inc, while LIC will offload 30.24% after the cabinet committee on economic affairs cleared the transaction on Wednesday. The sale comes with a lock-in period of five years with the Canadian company allowed to retain the brand for three years.

Article Title: Watsa's Prem-ium play in finance sector
Article Text:
Prem Watsa

NEW DELHI: Hyderabad-born Prem Watsa, chairman of Fairfax Financial Holdings, with assets of around $100 billion, has always been upbeat on India and its growth prospects.The Hyderabad Public School alumnus went to IIT Madras before pursuing an MBA in Canada, despite clearing the IIM entrance test.Watsa, now 75, was once apprehended by the police while rushing to make it to a job interview at Confederation Life as there was a bank robbery nearby. But he managed to get a job before moving to Gardiner Watson 11 years later. In 1984, Watsa and Tony Hamblin, his former boss at Confederation Life, set up Hamblin Watsa Investment Counsel. Fairfax was formed in 1985 after Watsa refinanced a Canadian insurance company and changed the name to Fairfax Financial, derived from the principles of fair and friendly acquisitions.He will have to put the principle to full use as he navigates the transition at IDBI Bank , once a development financial institution.Watsa is a big backer of financial services in India with Fairfax India, set up in 2014, portfolio reflecting that. Of the 13 investments, five were in the BFSI space, comprising 29% of the portfolio.The 75-year-old investor's latest bet - a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank for $5.6 billion- will further tilt the balance of the India portfolio towards financial services.Fairfax India's last balance sheet spoke of the immense opportunity in the sector given low levels of financial inclusion.But it also means that Watsa - often referred to as Canada's Warren Buffet - and his team will have to rejig the portfolio in line with RBI regulations, including deciding the plan for Catholic Syrian Bank and Go Digit. IIFL Finance, IIFL Capital and 5paisa are also part of the portfolio. Beyond finance, currently, Bangalore International Airport is Fairfax's biggest bet in India.Watsa is known for value-investing and looking for long-term returns. Fairfax India remains bullish on the economy. "In our view, India remains a land of immense opportunity!" its annual report said.
Article Summary: Prem Watsa is the chairman of Fairfax Financial Holdings, with assets of around $100 billion. The 75-year-old investor's latest bet - a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank for $5.6 billion- will further tilt the balance of the India portfolio towards financial services.

Article Title: Government tops divestment target of Rs 80k crore
Article Text: NEW DELHI: With over five months to go for the fiscal year to close, Centre has topped its disinvestment and asset monetisation target of Rs 80,000 crore for 2026-27, with its kitty swelling to Rs 88,665 crore once the IDBI Bank stake sale is completed - providing much-needed cushion in a year, when it is burdened with higher fuel and fertiliser subsidies.The Rs 26,500 crore from the IDBI transaction will add to the Rs 55,757 crore it has already raised from share sales, including the mega offer for sale of LIC shares that raked in over Rs 31,000 crore. Besides, it has mopped up Rs 6,367 crore through asset monetisation.While more share sales on exchanges are under process, Rs 15,000-20,000 crore is targeted to be generated from InvITs, involving highways. There has also been talk of monetising some of the stadiums in the capital but it is still on the drawing board. There is uncertainty around the much-delayed transaction involving Hotel Ashok due to security concerns.Even dividend flow is strong, with RBI announcing record dividend of nearly Rs 2.9 lakh crore and banks expected to deliver a bumper payout amid strong growth. RBI, banks and financial institutions were budgeted to pay just under Rs 3.2 lakh crore as dividends this year. Separately, PSUs have deposited Rs 17,773 crore in the treasury.Officials said the revenue situation is also looking comfortabl,e with direct taxes showing steady rise, while GST is so far above target. Despite the hit due to reduction in levies on petrol, the Centre appears on course to better the indirect tax target.
Article Summary: Centre has topped its disinvestment and asset monetisation target of Rs 80,000 crore for 2026-27. Its kitty will swell to Rs 88,665 crore once the IDBI Bank stake sale is completed. The Rs 26,500 crore from IDBI transaction will add to the Rs 55,757 crore it has already raised from share sales.

Article Title: Rupee rises for 4th day, up 19 paise vs dollar
Article Text:
Rupee slips 4 paise to 96.39 against US dollar

MUMBAI: The rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar on Wednesday, registering the fourth straight session of gains, supported by RBI interventions designed to ease near-term dollar demand and limit speculative foreign exchange exposure.Forex traders said the Indian rupee rose to a one-month high on RBI's measures to curb speculative bets. A weak dollar and easing of US Treasury yields also aided the rupee. However, weak domestic markets capped sharp gains. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 95.05 against the dollar and touched the intraday low of 94.76 against the greenback.On Tuesday, the rupee strengthened for the third straight session and appreciated 42 paise to close at 95.36. In the last four trading sessions, the rupee has gained 171 paise . "We expect the rupee to trade with a positive bias on RBI's intervention to curb excessive speculation in the rupee. A weak dollar and a decline in US Treasury yields may also support the rupee," an analyst said. Agencies
Article Summary: Rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar on Wednesday. It was the fourth straight session of gains, supported by RBI interventions. A weak dollar and easing of US Treasury yields also aided the rupee. However, weak domestic markets capped sharp gains.

Article Title: Jio Platforms files papers, IPO set to open on October 21
Article Text: MUMBAI: Reliance Industries (RIL) on Wednesday said that the initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms will open on Oct 21 and close on Oct 23. Jio Platforms, the holding company for the Mukesh Ambani-controlled group's telecom and digital initiatives, will offer about 27 crore shares in the IPO at a per-share price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119, translating to fund mobilisation of about Rs 30,213 crore.This offer size will make the issue the largest IPO in India, surpassing the Rs 27,860-crore offer by Hyundai Motor India in Oct 2024.With nearly 921 crore shares outstanding, at the upper limit of the price band, Jio Platforms will have a market capitalisation of about Rs 10.3 lakh crore.Going by current market cap ranking on BSE, this will make Jio Platforms the fourth most valued company in India, behind RIL (Rs 15.9 lakh crore), Bharti Airtel (Rs 11.2 lakh crore) and HDFC Bank (almost at Rs 11 lakh crore). In terms of market cap, Jio Platforms will be ahead of ICICI Bank, SBI and TCS, data from BSE showed.RIL is the main promoter of Jio Platforms with a 66.4% holding in the company. Global giants like Google, Meta (parent of Facebook), KKR, ADIA and General Atlantic are also among the minority shareholders of the company, IPO papers filed with Sebi showed.Unlike some of the largest issues in India in recent times, none of the existing shareholders in the company are selling any shares in the offer.On Wednesday, Jio Platforms filed the IPO papers with the Registrar of Companies, Gujarat, in Ahmedabad, RIL said in a disclosure to the exchanges. In the IPO, Rs 500 crore worth of shares are reserved for eligible employees of the company while Rs 2,500 crore worth of shares are reserved for eligible shareholders of RIL, it said. The anchor investor bidding date is Monday, Oct 19. The IPO will open for subscription on Wednesday, Oct 21 and close on Friday, Oct 23, the RIL disclosure said. In the IPO, investors can bid in lots of 12 Jio Platforms shares and multiples of the same. The company is slotted to be listed on the bourses on Oct 28.On Wednesday evening, the grey market premium (GMP) for Jio Platforms shares was at Rs 200, slightly down from Tuesday's level of Rs 218 but much ahead of its Oct 4 level at Rs 148. GMP is the mark-up that speculators in the unofficial market for IPO-bound shares are willing to bid for when the shares are listed.
Article Summary: Reliance Industries (RIL) on Wednesday said that the initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms will open on Oct 21 and close on Oct 23. The holding company for the Mukesh Ambani-controlled group's telecom and digital initiatives, will offer about 27 crore shares in the IPO at a per-share price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119.

Article Title: IDBI sale to increase value, new management to get free hand
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The sale of govt stake in IDBI Bank will help increase its value, fully protect the interest of employees and directors nominated by the Centre and LIC will exit the board to give the new management a free hand, a top govt official told TOI on Wednesday.Hours after govt nod, Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla also vowed to move ahead with other transactions in the coming months and "not rest on past laurels". "We still haven't finished our work. We are further energised by the approval... We will continue to move ahead with the strategic transactions, and we will take Cabinet approvals to their logical conclusions. You will keep hearing from us from time to time," he said, without commenting on specific companies.Since 2016, the Union Cabinet has cleared three dozen strategic transactions but several of them, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation are no longer being pursued. Chawla dismissed suggestions that govt was not keen on privatisation of PSUs. "We are delivering on what has been approved by the Cabinet and we have completed five strategic sales in the last five years... Govt remains firmly on the track of reforms.The secretary said the new owners will bring fresh energy and private sector management practices and efficiency to boost IDBI Bank's performance, while expecting the transaction to be closed before end of the current financial year."We have spent the last one year discussing with the management, the employee associations, the qualified parties. We've brought everyone on board. Even today the service conditions of the IDBI Bank employees is decided by its board. The service conditions of all existing employees will be fully protected, all pensioners of IDBI Bank will be fully protected. There is a special pension fund set aside for this purpose and going forward, the new management will run the bank in consultation with the employees and its associations. "Chawla said a lot of hard work has gone into ensuring that the transaction was cleared. After the setback in March, when the bids were rejected, the core group on transactions led by the Cabinet secretary and DIPAM went back to the drawing board. "We relied completely on professional advice. When the stock market price is extremely volatile and the stock is very narrowly traded, it tends to misalign the intrinsic value," he said.So, govt studied global examples and went for relative valuation by what is called market multiple method or moon charts methodology. The market multiples of comparable entities are used to compute the fair market value. Separately, an asset valuation method was used based on the assets and liabilities."Because the book value of IDBI Bank was low, the professional agencies converted the asset and liabilities on the books, including financial assets and physical assets like land and buildings, into their fair replacement value. In addition, they valued intangibles like the economic value of the banking licence, customer relationship, which is built on its branch network, the brand value and added all this up to the book value to arrive at the net asset value or the fair value asset value," Chawla added.Using the average of the two valuations worked out to Rs 75.99 a share, while the winning best bid was Rs 81 a share, resulting in CCEA clearing the Farifax offer."After six months of hard work and through a collective decision and multi-lauyered decision making process, where everyone's views were taken on board and professional agencies were allowed to do their job, we have been able to find a way forward... We have stood up to take difficult decisions and that is what is necessary to drive reforms."
Article Summary: Since 2016, the Union Cabinet has cleared three dozen strategic transactions but several of them, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation are no longer being pursued. Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla also vowed to move ahead with other transactions in the coming months and "not rest on past laurels"

Article Title: Wholesale inflation touches 30-month high
Article Text: New Delhi: Factory gate inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) surged to a 30 month high of 11.4% in Sept from 9.9% in Aug, as rising fuel and manufactured goods prices pushed inflation into double digits, the official data released Wednesday showed. In comparison, WPI stood at -0.2% in Sept 2025.Data shows fuel and power inflation accelerated to 25.9% in Sept from 22.9% in Aug as prices for crude petroleum, natural gas and mineral oil continued to rise, amid uncertainty surrounding key maritime chokepoints due to renewed hostilities in West Asia.Inflation in manufactured products, which account for nearly two-thirds of the WPI basket, rose to 9.8% from 8.4% in Aug, with acceleration being particularly sharp in basic metals (17%), chemicals and chemical products (16.7%), textiles and rubber products (13.7%) and electrical equipment (12%).CareEdge chief economist Rajani Sinha said India's crude basket and spot brent crude prices are trading well above brent futures, indicating tightness in the physical supply of crude. "While retail fuel prices have remained unchanged, oil marketing companies have raised bulk diesel prices, which are now nearly Rs 50-60 per litre higher than retail prices. Persistently elevated crude prices could increase freight, agricultural and irrigation and transportation costs, which could indirectly feed into the retail inflation," she added.Food prices also contributed to the Sept increase as WPI Food Index rose to 8.7% from 7.1% in Aug, continuing an upward trend seen over recent month.Though RBI tracks consumer price index (CPI) based retail inflation for its policy rate setting, the former tends to feed into the latter, albeit with a lag. Official data released Monday showed retail inflation inching to 5.5% in Sept from 4.8% in Aug.
Article Summary: Factory gate inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) surged to a 30 month high of 11.4% in Sept from 9.9% in Aug. In comparison, WPI stood at -0.2% in September 2025. Data shows fuel and power inflation accelerated to 25.9%.

Article Title: Currency depreciation key headwind for foreign investors: Blackstone's Gray
Article Text:
Despite being the fastest-growing large economy, India is witnessing capital outflows. What ails foreign investment?

Does currency depreciation worry you? What needs to be done?

Last year, you spoke about making delisting easier...

In AI, which areas would you look at investing in?

What risks do you see in AI investments?

But telecom companies did take a hit when Starlink announced its foray into telecom...

You earlier spoke about risks arising from conflicts and macro factors. At the same time, many countries, including India, are seeing unrest. Do you see this impacting business?

MUMBAI: Its $50 billion investments in India place Blackstone among the top 10 business houses. The world's largest alternative asset manager plans to double its investments in the next five years mainly in private equity and real estate, and expand into infrastructure, credit and growth investing. In an interview with TOI, Jonathan Gray, president and COO of Blackstone, speaks of how the focus is on building businesses.The energy-price shock from the war, rising interest rates, AI disruption fears in IT services and India's once-high market valuations have triggered a correction. Yet, underlying growth remains strong, with the PM citing nearly 8% economic growth and market earnings expected to rise at mid-teens rates in Q3.For long-term investors, the reset offers a better entry point, with lower valuations improving opportunities for new capital. Markets may turn fickle, but sustained earnings growth should draw global capital back. We see this as a temporary cold patch and will continue investing.Currency depreciation has been the biggest headwind for foreign investors, making faster-growing businesses a better bet than bond-like assets with flat returns.We focus on high-growth healthcare, financial services, travel, digital infrastructure and real estate, including malls, offices and warehouses. India has made major strides in physical infrastructure, from airports and flyovers to GST reform, digital payments, legal systems and capital markets. These improvements have opened sectors once inaccessible to investors like us. So, rather than focus only on what govt can do better, it is important to stop and say they have done a heck of a job.India's 90% shareholding threshold for delisting is among the world's highest. Some of the rules are there to protect minority shareholders from promoters, but I think there's a way to do that and allow some of these companies to be privatised (delisted). Reforms can unlock consolidation, reward shareholders and improve companies' access to capital, as Japan's liberalisation has shown. It is like refreshing the farm by turning the soil.Yet, there have been some major capital-market strides. The REIT market, once non-existent, has attracted billions in capital, enabled us to bring five out of six REITs to the market and a $1.3 billion secondary sale in Knowledge Realty Trust in Aug. India is the world's second-most liquid IPO market after the US. Greater regulatory and tax certainty remains a work in progress, but govt deserves credit for opening markets to foreign capital. Further reforms could deepen access to capital.AI opportunities span data centres, neoclouds and IT services. As traditional IT work shifts to AI, firms such as Mphasis, in which we own a large stake, are becoming AI-deployment partners, helping businesses redesign workflows rather than simply adopt tools such as Claude. Energy, especially renewables, will also be critical to powering both India's growth and its expanding data-centre infra.There is a risk of overinvestment and capital misallocation in AI, but financial commentary is too negative. Usage is surging, with tangible productivity gains. At IGI, our diamond and jewellery certification business in India, AI visualisation tools make grading 40% faster and enable each employee to process 30% more diamonds.Demand is exploding, driven by businesses and individuals using personalised AI agents, while computing capacity remains constrained by shortages of land, power, chips and capital. Unlike the '90s telecom boom, when speculative, leveraged infrastructure outstripped demand, today's data-centre build-out has strong demand, investment-grade hyperscalers as offtakers and little speculative construction. It is therefore financially sounder than booms seen in the past.AI's biggest risk is disruption to legacy businesses, already reflected in falling software and professional-services valuations and questions over the future of billable hours. Some AI investments will fail, but the technology's productivity gains and growth potential make significant infrastructure investment compelling.Investment in computing infrastructure can be compared to aviation, where aircraft retain value despite airline failures. Likewise, scarce AI computing capacity can be redeployed if an LLM company, software firm or hyperscaler fails. Markets may underestimate this residual value. Most data centres are backed by 15-20-year contracts with trillion-dollar-plus companies, limiting speculative, leveraged construction.In a world connected by social media, we have seen a rise in social unrest, and I think that's going to be more of a staple of societies going forward because organising is now much easier. Part of it is also that we have seen a sharp rise in the cost of living, energy costs, food costs and housing costs, and I think this is something govts are going to need to respond to. I think in the West, we've made it very difficult to build new energy, new infrastructure and new housing, and I hope there's a push for some regulatory and permitting reform to accelerate investment in those areas. Technological upheaval also breeds anxiety, as during past industrial revolutions, while wars add to cost pressures. Hopefully, these wars will end at some point, and that should reduce pressure on prices. Economic growth is critical to getting countries through this, and countries will have to control the cost of living through fiscal discipline and low inflation.
Article Summary: Jonathan Gray, president and COO of Blackstone, speaks of how the focus is on building businesses. India is the world's second-most liquid IPO market after the US. Greater regulatory and tax certainty remains a work in progress. Further reforms could deepen access to capital.

Article Title: Groww Q2 profit up 54% to Rs 725 cr
Article Text:
BENGALURU

: Online investment platform Groww’s net profit rose 54% from a year earlier to Rs 725 crore for the September quarter. Its revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore, with margin lending and commodity derivatives contributing a larger share.Sequentially, however, net profit fell 1.4% from Rs 735 crore in the June quarter, while revenue dipped 0.5% from Rs 1,549 crore.The company is also testing a US stock investing product, co-founder and CEO Lalit Keshre told analysts. He described it as a very early test and said there was no fixed timeline for a launch. “The feedback is really good from the customers,” he said, adding that Groww would continue refining the product based on their responses.Equity derivatives revenue fell 14.3% from the previous quarter. Groww attributed most of the decline to market adjustments following Sebi’s introduction of a closing auction system in August, which changed how closing prices are determined for certain stocks. The segment remained its biggest income contributor, but its share fell to 44.8% from 56.9% a year earlier.Management said proposed changes to derivatives settlement could help normalise trading activity.It cautioned that volumes would also depend on factors such as market volatility.Meanwhile, Groww’s outstanding margin trading loan book grew to Rs 4,351 crore from Rs 1,668 crore a year earlier. The facility allows customers to borrow funds to buy shares.Chief financial officer Ishan Bansal said Groww had tightened its lending policies and was examining exposure to individual stocks across the industry, alongside its own positions.“We have to start looking at the industry level book as well,” he said. Groww is excluding some stocks from its approved lending list or requiring higher margins. In some cases, Bansal said, it finances only 20% of the value, limiting its exposure if prices fall sharply.Expenses rose 29% to Rs 556 crore. Technology costs increased because of more trading days, greater use of AI and higher computing costs. Groww also incurred Rs 13 crore in one-time client reimbursements following an operational issue at a third-party market infrastructure institution. Management said delayed files on an expiry day had caused the issue.Marketing spending fell sequentially because IPL-related expenses incurred in the June quarter did not recur. Management said it typically spends Rs 400–500 crore annually on growth, with spending adjusted to market conditions.IPO activity helped Groww add 11 lakh new transacting users during the quarter. Total customer assets across its platforms rose 46% to Rs 3.9 lakh crore.
Article Summary: Groww’s net profit rose 54% from a year earlier to Rs 725 crore for the September quarter. Its revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore, with margin lending and commodity derivatives contributing a larger share. The company is also testing a US stock investing product.

Article Title: Who is Neha Bora? From Delhi University to JNU, the education and activism of AISA’s president
Article Text:
Who is Neha Bora? Know about her education, PhD research and journey from theatre to student politics

Educational journey from Delhi University to JNU

Theatre and the beginning of activism

The 23-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar

Recent protests and detention in Delhi

Neha Bora, the 29-year-old national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), has drawn national attention for her participation in student-led protests, including a recent demonstration in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A doctoral scholar at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), Bora combines academic research in theatre and performance studies with political activism. Her recent detention after a dash towards Connaught Place, following an agitation called near RK Ashram Marg Metro station, brought her activities into the public spotlight.Born in Khatima, Uttarakhand, Bora grew up moving between cities because her father served in the Indian Army. She completed her schooling in Bengal, where she encountered the writings and political ideas of Charu Majumdar, Pablo Neruda and Arundhati Roy.Bora graduated in sociology from Hindu College, University of Delhi, before pursuing postgraduate studies at Dr B. R. Ambedkar University. She subsequently joined JNU’s School of Arts and Aesthetics for a PhD in theatre and performance studies.Bora’s involvement in public causes developed through theatre.During her time at Delhi University, she participated in plays addressing social issues and later became associated with Sangwari, a Delhi-based street theatre group. She has described her transition from theatre to politics as an organic progression.The 2019 protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act also influenced her political engagement. She later joined AISA, a Left-wing student organisation associated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation, and became its national president.Bora joined fellow student leaders Manish Kumar and Aameen Amitoj in a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar alongside activist Sonam Wangchuk. The three continued their fast for 23 days before ending it on July 20 following appeals from MPs, activists and public figures. Reports said Bora lost eight kilograms during the protest.The agitation highlighted opposition to the National Education Policy, 2020 and the centralisation of competitive examinations, issues she says have fuelled student concerns for years.On Sunday, October 11, Bora led supporters towards Connaught Place after police action around the protest gathering. She announced their arrival on social media at 2.51pm and was detained shortly afterwards.In a video posted on X, she alleged that protesters faced cramped conditions and mistreatment inside a police bus. Police had not responded to these allegations in the reports available.Bora also participated in protests in Jharkhand, where ink was thrown at her near the state Assembly on August 7. Her speeches have attracted controversy, including police complaints over remarks concerning Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
Article Summary: Neha Bora is the national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) She has drawn national attention for her participation in student-led protests. A doctoral scholar at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Bora combines academic research in theatre and performance studies with political activism.

Article Title: Amid AI push, no internet in 48% of Karnataka schools
Article Text:
Karnataka is introducing AI skills in schools, with significant challenges in internet accessibility (AI image)





BENGALURU: While Karnataka is favouring introduction of AI skills and coding in its schools, nearly 48% of the state’s 74,578 schools do not have internet connectivity, exposing a glaring digital divide.According to UDISE+ report released by Union ministry of education for 2025–26, the state’s connectivity rate is well below the national average of 67%. Nearly one in three schools in India lacks internet access, while every second school in Karnataka lacks the facility.Home to the country’s IT capital, Karnataka has the highest percentage of schools without internet connectivity among the southern states — both as a proportion of total schools and in absolute numbers.The gap is particularly alarming in government schools. Of the state’s 48,527 government-managed schools, only 18,007 have internet facilities, leaving about 30,520 (63%) without connectivity.These contrasting figures come at a time when chief minister DK Shivakumar, during his Independence Day, announced the AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula initiatives across Karnataka, aimed at introducing AI education in schools from Class 6.Subsequently, the CM said AI training had already begun for Class 9 students in govt schools and directed officials to explore extending it to younger students, with support from the information technology department and private organisations. However, the widening infrastructure gap raises questions about how uniformly these initiatives can be implemented across the state.D Shashi Kumar, general secretary of the Associated Managements of Primary and Secondary Schools in Karnataka (KAMS), pointed out that the digital divide could widen if the number of schools with functional internet connections were considered, as several schools reporting internet access do not have an active connection.“AI education requires access to computers, suitable software, trained teachers and, for many learning applications, reliable internet connectivity. Without these basic facilities, students in poorly connected schools risk being left behind even as their peers gain exposure to emerging technologies. Although the government has pinned its hopes on CSR initiatives, how many schools will these initiatives cover? All these programmes require substantial financial resources. Will the government be able to provide the necessary funds?” he asked.Karnataka’s performance is also poor compared with that of its southern neighbours. Andhra Pradesh has internet access in 99.2% of its 60,843 schools, while Tamil Nadu has achieved 99% coverage across 57,566 schools. Kerala reports connectivity in 92.6% of its 15,750 schools. Telangana, despite having a sizeable gap of its own, has internet access in 76.5% of its 41,762 schools. Karnataka, with connectivity in just 51.7% of its schools, has the lowest coverage in South India, the report revealed.“The proportion of schools without internet connectivity in Karnataka is more than twice that of Telangana, where 23.5% of schools lack access, and over six times the national average of 32.6%,” a Bengaluru-based academician said.Nationally, 4.77 lakh of India’s 14.67 lakh schools lack internet access, according to the report. Karnataka accounts for approximately 7.5% of the nationwide deficit.
Article Summary: Nearly 48% of the state’s 74,578 schools do not have internet connectivity, exposing a glaring digital divide. Nearly one in three schools in India lacks internet access, while every second school in Karnataka lacks the facility. Karnataka has the highest percentage of schools without internet connectivity among the southern states.

Article Title: ‘Their fault? Unfurling Tricolour’: Abhijeet Dipke hits out as CJP leaders sent to 5-day judicial custody
Article Text:
Abhjeet Dipke slams 5-day judicial custody for Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka

Why were CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka sent to judicial custody?

CJP objects to Jantar Mantar being denotified as protest site





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi after party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody, alleging that the action was aimed at suppressing dissent.Dipke claimed that the two leaders’ only fault was unfurling the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar and challenged Modi to formally declare an Emergency if the government intended to curb protests.In a post on X, Dipke accused the government of using coercive measures against those demonstrating against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Ashu and Saurav have been sent to 5 days judicial custody. Their fault? Unfurling tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Show some guts, @narendramodi. If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics,” he posted.Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody after being detained early Tuesday for allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, which was recently denotified as a designated protest site.The two allegedly raised slogans demanding Kumar’s resignation.Police registered a case against them on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties.Das and Ranka had signed bonds undertaking to maintain peace for a year after being detained during an earlier protest in the capital on Saturday, officials said.The latest action comes amid a continuing standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over the venue for demonstrations against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar issued an order designating Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for protests and demonstrations, following which Jantar Mantar was removed from the list of designated protest sites.The CJP has criticised the decision, arguing that shifting demonstrations away from the political centre of the national capital would diminish the visibility of public dissent.The party has continued to demand Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke criticises Prime Minister Narendra Modi. CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody. Dipke claimed that the two leaders’ only fault was unfurling Tricolour at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: US stocks fall as inflation accelerates; S&P 500 drops 1.1%, Nasdaq slides 1.6%
Article Text:
Investors also weighed the risks and potential returns of heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Wall Street stocks fell on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected US inflation data pushed Treasury yields higher, adding to concerns about borrowing costs even as major banks assessed the opportunities and risks associated with the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom.The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, putting it on track for its fifth decline in six sessions since hitting a record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 171 points, or 0.3%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 1.6%, as of 1:14 pm Eastern time.US consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6%. The data fuelled concerns that inflation could remain elevated, partly due to rising energy prices amid the war with Iran.The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 5.23%, after briefly crossing 5.32% during the session. Higher yields can weigh on equities by increasing borrowing costs and making bonds more attractive relative to stocks.Meanwhile, executives at major US banks highlighted the opportunities presented by AI infrastructure investment, while cautioning that uncertainty over demand, financing costs and returns could create risks.Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said the long-term demand for capital and computing capacity required by the AI ecosystem remained uncertain.“No one knows how the demands for capital and compute will evolve as the broader AI ecosystem matures,” Solomon said, stressing the need for vigilance in financing decisions and risk management.Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser, however, said investment in the broader AI ecosystem was not slowing, citing an ongoing shortage of computing capacity.The AI infrastructure expansion, driven by heavy investment in data centres and computing power, presents banks with opportunities to finance large-scale projects. However, elevated interest rates could raise project costs, squeeze returns and make debt repayment more difficult.Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf described the AI buildout as a significant economic force, bringing both opportunities and risks because of the substantial borrowing involved and pressure on prices across some industries and supply chains.Banks are also deploying AI internally to improve productivity and reduce costs, although the financial benefits vary. Fraser said Citi was developing products up to 40% faster using AI and had reduced technology vendor expenses by 30% through coding tools.Investors are watching whether such efficiency gains can justify the heavy spending on AI. Concerns are also mounting over cybersecurity threats and the risks posed by AI agents capable of taking actions autonomously.The combination of persistent inflation, elevated bond yields and uncertainty over AI investment returns has added to the challenges facing Wall Street, where high stock valuations leave limited room for corporate earnings or productivity gains to disappoint.
Article Summary: US consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, accelerating from 3.4% in August and exceeding economists’ expectations of 3.6%. The data fuelled concerns that inflation could remain elevated, partly due to rising energy prices amid the war with Iran. Investors also weighed the risks and potential returns of heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Article Title: US inflation accelerates to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices surge
Article Text:
This the sharpest increase in five months, as higher fuel costs and persistent underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden

Gasoline prices drive inflation

Core inflation also picks up

What it means for Federal Reserve

US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for American households ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7 per cent year-on-year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August, the US Labor Department said on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.6 per cent, compared with a 0.4 per cent rise in the previous month.The annual inflation rate was slightly above economists' expectations of 3.6 per cent, according to a Reuters poll, while the monthly increase was in line with forecasts.The latest figures reflect the impact of higher energy costs following the US-Israeli war with Iran, which began in late February and disrupted oil and gas supplies. Rising costs have added to concerns over affordability, a key issue ahead of the midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is seeking to retain control of Congress.Gasoline prices were a major contributor to the monthly increase in consumer prices, rising sharply in September.US Energy Information Administration data showed gasoline prices climbed 7.1 per cent during the month, while the Labor Department's CPI report recorded a 9.1 per cent increase.Higher fuel costs have also pushed up expenses across other sectors, including transportation and travel. Airfares rose 1.2 per cent in September and were up around 22 per cent from a year earlier, while hotel prices increased 2 per cent over the month.Rising fuel and transportation expenses have also increased costs for businesses, raising the risk that companies will pass some of the additional burden on to consumers through higher prices for goods and services.Grocery prices offered some relief, declining 0.1 per cent in September, although they remained 1.8 per cent higher than a year earlier.Underlying price pressures remained firm even after excluding volatile food and energy components. Core CPI rose 2.6 per cent in September from a year earlier, compared with 2.4 per cent in August.On a monthly basis, core inflation increased 0.3 per cent, matching the previous month's rise. Price increases across a range of goods and services suggest that inflationary pressures extend beyond the energy sector.Economists have also pointed to strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centres as a factor pushing up the cost of semiconductors, computer equipment and electronic devices.“The report was worse than expected,” Bill Adams, chief US economist at Fifth Third Bank, said in a note to clients, adding that price increases were widespread across durable goods, nondurable goods and services.The inflation data could complicate the Federal Reserve's decisions on interest rates as policymakers weigh persistent price pressures against the impact of tighter monetary policy on economic growth.The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points last month to a range of 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent, marking its first rate increase in three years. It has indicated that further increases could follow if inflation remains elevated.Financial markets had assigned a roughly 22 per cent probability of another rate increase at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting before the September CPI report, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.However, some economists expect policymakers to hold rates steady at the upcoming meeting and assess further economic data before deciding on another increase. Higher borrowing costs can help moderate demand and slow price increases, but they cannot directly address supply disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts.The latest inflation figures come as the cost of living remains a major concern for American voters ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The September inflation report is also important for millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits. The annual cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 is based on inflation data for urban wage earners and clerical workers during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.5 per cent increase in Social Security benefits for 2027, up from the 2.8 per cent adjustment for 2026. The Social Security Administration is expected to announce the official adjustment later on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7 per cent year-on-year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.6 per cent, compared with a 0.4% rise in the previous month. Rising costs have added to concerns over affordability, a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

Article Title: Oil prices climb as Houthis step up attacks on Saudi Arabia, stoking supply fears
Article Text:
Oil prices rise to to $106.58 a barrel (AI-generated image)

Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed the risk of supply disruptions from escalating attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia against expectations of increased Russian diesel exports easing market tightness.Brent crude futures rose 89 cents, or 0.8%, to $106.58 a barrel by 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 80 cents, or 0.9%, to $94.94. Brent had fallen 0.9% on Tuesday, while WTI gained 0.4%.“Supply concern stemming from conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is driving prices higher,” Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, told Reuters. He said expectations of increased Russian diesel exports could limit sharp price movements in either direction.Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said the Houthis attacked an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in Dhahran, causing a limited fire. The group has launched ballistic missiles and drones at the kingdom over the past week in retaliation for Riyadh’s support for Yemeni government forces.US president Donald Trump accused the Houthis of deliberately trying to drive up oil prices ahead of the US midterm elections.In a post on Truth Social on Tuesday, he said the group had re-emerged, probably at Iran’s behest, and warned that he would not forget the attacks after the elections.Trump also threatened to step up US military action in the Middle East after the November elections, which will determine whether Republicans retain their majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia increased oil production last month despite disruptions to shipments caused by the US-Iran war, contributing to a sharp rise in output from OPEC+, the oil producers’ alliance, according to data cited by Reuters.Iran is also deploying new tactics to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.In a potential counterweight to supply concerns, Russia said on Tuesday it saw no direct link between peace talks with Ukraine and its deal to export diesel to the US. The statement followed a report that US envoys had told Ukrainian officials the deal was part of an effort to bring Moscow back to negotiations.Analysts expect the competing pressures from regional conflict and potential increases in fuel supply to shape oil price movements in the coming days.
